transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-28
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48m
Attendees: Maya Park (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Sophie Patel (Redwood Solutions), Ethan Morales (Northfield Head of Search), Priya Desai (Eng Manager), Jules Carter (Data Platform), Ava Nguyen (Security)

Summary (auto): Intro, scope, constraints, next steps noted.

[00:00] Maya Park: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro from our side, I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, Liam's our SE who will run the deep parts.
[00:12] Ethan Morales: Thanks Maya. Quick context: we're redoing our product search ranking and want to move to an embeddings + rerank flow. Current infra is Postgres + some classic BM25 and a homegrown vector pipeline using Faiss on a few instances.
[00:25] Priya Desai: We're seeing p95s spike when fanout hits 20-30 candidates. Looking for ways to reduce overall cost but keep or improve relevance.
[00:33] Liam Chen: Got it. High level: Redwood supports hosted, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem. For embeddings and rerank you'd usually decide based on throughput predictability and data residency. Can you share numbers for QPS and vector dims?
[00:48] Jules Carter: Right now we index ~10M items, embeddings at 1536 dims—openai-style embeddings—and QPS average 120, peak 450 during promos. Tail latency requirement p95 < 200ms if possible, p99 ideally < 500ms.
[01:05] Maya Park: That's a helpful baseline. Two decisions packed in here: where to run embeddings and rerank, and how to integrate with your vector DB. A common pattern is hybrid: do a cheap embed similarity fanout from a vector DB then rerank top-K with a Redwood generation/rerank model. Saves cost vs reranking the whole corpus.
[01:22] Ethan Morales: Our concerns: network egress costs if hosted, plus compliance—some docs are regulated. Also curious how quantization affects recall at 1536 dims.
[01:34] Ava Nguyen: From security side we'd need SOC2, support for SSO (SAML/Okta), audit logs, and KMS for keys if we go private. We may need VPC peering if hosted.
[01:46] Liam Chen: That's doable. Hosted supports private networking options for enterprise tiers, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with isolation, and Private gives customer-managed control plane. We can provide SOC2 report and audit logs; KMS integrations available. For strict air-gapped workflows we recommend Private on-prem.
[02:05] Priya Desai: On the vector DB side we're considering switching from Faiss to Milvus or Pinecone to reduce ops. How do those integrate? Do you host the index or do we?
[02:18] Maya Park: Redwood typically integrates both ways. You can keep your vector DB in your VPC and call Redwood for rerank/generation via VPC peering, or you can push vectors to a cloud-hosted vector DB and call both services. For the fanout-first pattern we recommend keeping the index close to where vectors are generated to minimize network hops.
[02:36] Jules Carter: If we keep the index in our VPC and call Redwood for rerank, what's the latency tradeoff? Our p95 budget is tight.
[02:45] Liam Chen: Latency has two components: fanout vector search and rerank. If vector search is in your VPC and rerank in Redwood hosted, you'll see network RTT. For our Dedicated customers we run rerank in the same region and can colocate; with Private you avoid RTTs and egress. For your 450 QPS peak and p95 <200ms, Dedicated or Private are safer if low tail latency is required. Hosted can work with caching and prefix KV cache to lower token costs and latency, but network requirements and throughput burst patterns matter.
[03:12] Ethan Morales: What's the guidance on dimensionality? We could reduce vectors to 512 dims with PCA or train new smaller embeddings. How big a recall hit would we see?
[03:22] Liam Chen: Dimensionality depends on your semantic granularity. 1536 is high-fidelity; going to 512 often reduces recall slightly but can be recovered with rerank on the top-K. Quantization (int8/4-bit) for storage can be very effective; we have profiles showing minimal recall impact for dense retrieval when combined with rerank. We'll share eval numbers.
[03:42] Maya Park: For a pilot, a pragmatic approach: 1) keep current 1536 vectors in your DB, 2) run a fanout to top-200, 3) rerank with a lightweight model for top-20. That reduces rerank cost and keeps recall. We can propose configs for vector size/quantization tradeoffs.
[03:58] Priya Desai: Cost wise, how does Redwood bill for rerank and embeddings? Per-token and per-embedding units? And for Dedicated, is it a monthly reserved capacity?
[04:10] Maya Park: Hosted is usage-based (per-token, per-embedding), Dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly/annual) with predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale. Private has licensing plus infra. We'll send a cost model with sample numbers tuned to your QPS.
[04:25] Jules Carter: We have an ops constraint: limited ability to run large Faiss clusters. If we offload to Pinecone/Milvus, we want to avoid double-ops. Does Redwood manage indexes?
[04:36] Liam Chen: We don't manage your vector DB index unless it's part of a managed add-on. For most customers, we recommend keeping the vector index in your infra with connectors (we have integration examples for Milvus/Pinecone). For cost and complexity, many choose Pinecone as a managed index.
[04:50] Ethan Morales: Is there a benchmark we can run to emulate our load? We want to test throughput with 10M vectors and mixture of 70% search, 30% rerank workloads.
[04:59] Liam Chen: Yes. We'll provide a benchmark template and a client workload script to simulate fanout+rerank at your QPS. Recommended pilot: ingest a 10M sample set, run 24h smoke test at 60% of your peak, capture p95/p99. We'll instrument TTL caches and KV usage.
[05:18] Ava Nguyen: For security, if we do hosted with VPC peering, data flow goes from our VPC to Redwood over a private tunnel? What's encrypted, at rest and in transit?
[05:27] Maya Park: All transit is TLS. For hosted, we support private peering, and all data at rest can be encrypted using customer-managed keys (KMS). We'll include a diagram in the security pack.
[05:38] Priya Desai: What about model fallbacks? If we have an SLA and the primary model is saturated, can Redwood fallback to a smaller model automatically?
[05:46] Liam Chen: Yes. Smart routing policies can fallback to compatible model variants by policy (latency/cost/region). You can configure automatic fallback to a cheaper half-precision quantized model for non-critical traffic. That reduces outages and cost.
[05:58] Ethan Morales: Are there prebuilt rerank models you'd recommend or do we bring our own?
[06:03] Liam Chen: We have curated rerank models tuned for re-ranking top-K. You can also bring a fine-tuned model. For your use case, start with our normed rerank (small-medium size) and evaluate. It's cheaper to use our hosted ones during pilot.
[06:14] Maya Park: Quick note on caching: prefix/KV cache can dramatically reduce token cost for repeated queries; for high QPS with repeated or templated queries you'll see gains.
[06:22] Jules Carter: We do have a lot of templated queries from product pages. That could help.
[06:26] Priya Desai: Any gotchas with hybrid routing and fanout size? We worry about exploding costs when fanout is large.
[06:33] Liam Chen: Fanout sizing is a knob—top-50 vs top-200—balance cost and recall. We recommend an eval sweep: measure recall vs top-K and rerank cost vs latency. Also consider sharded vdb fanout to parallelize retrieval and reduce per-node latency.
[06:51] Ethan Morales: Can Redwood trace token-level costs back to query templates and routes?
[06:55] Maya Park: Yes, Redwood Console gives token-level cost breakdowns and per-route metrics so you can see per-query economics.
[07:02] Ava Nguyen: Last security question: audit logs retention and access controls? SSO and RBAC are musts for us.
[07:07] Maya Park: We support SSO (SAML/Okta), RBAC with granular roles, and configurable audit log retention for enterprise plans. We'll send the policy example.
[07:16] Priya Desai: This has been great. For the pilot, timeline wise we need results in two weeks to feed to execs. Is that feasible?
[07:24] Liam Chen: Two weeks for a scoped pilot (ingest sample, run smoke test, analyze) is tight but doable if we scope to 10M vectors and 24-48h runs. We'll prep the benchmark and stick to the target.
[07:36] Maya Park: Recap and next steps: Redwood sends security pack (SOC2, KMS doc), benchmarking template and client script, and a cost model. Northfield shares query histograms and confirms whether they want Hosted+Dedicates hybrid or Private. We'll schedule a follow-up technical deep dive with Priya and Jules.
[07:55] Ethan Morales: Sounds good. We'll aim to confirm the hosting preference by 9/10. Thanks everyone.
[08:02] Maya Park: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
